core_obligations: Produce the long exact cohomology sequence of the short exact sequence 0 -> (M_1, N_1, phi_1, psi_1) -> (M_2, N_2, phi_2, psi_2) -> (M_3, N_3, phi_3, psi_3) -> 0 of 2-periodic complexes, and truncate it to the finite exact sequence 0 -> I -> H^0(A) -> H^0(B) -> H^0(C) -> H^1(A) -> H^1(B) -> K -> 0, with 0 -> K -> H^1(C) -> I -> 0 as the accompanying filtration (proof lines 228-251).

Read off finiteness: if two of the three complexes have finite-length cohomology, the exact sequence shows the remaining cohomology modules are finite length too, so all terms occurring in the displayed finite exact sequence have a well-defined length (proof lines 242-252).

Apply additivity of the length function to the displayed finite exact sequence to obtain e_R(B) = e_R(A) + e_R(C), which is exactly the asserted identity e_R(M_2, N_2, phi_2, psi_2) = e_R(M_1, N_1, phi_1, psi_1) + e_R(M_3, N_3, phi_3, psi_3) (proof lines 252-254).
proof_roadmap: Abbreviate the three complexes as A, B, C and write down the long exact cohomology sequence of the given short exact sequence (proof lines 228-241).
Reorganise the long exact sequence into a finite exact sequence with one filtration, using that only H^0 and H^1 occur for a 2-periodic complex (proof lines 242-251).
Apply additivity of length to that finite exact sequence, which is precisely the stated additivity of e_R (proof lines 252-254).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that e_R is additive in short exact sequences of 2-periodic complexes, with the additional statement that finite length of two out of three cohomology modules forces it for the third (statement lines 210-224). The work is to package the long exact cohomology sequence of the given short exact sequence into the finite exact sequence 0 -> I -> H^0(A) -> H^0(B) -> H^0(C) -> H^1(A) -> H^1(B) -> K -> 0 together with the filtration 0 -> K -> H^1(C) -> I -> 0, so that the alternating sum of lengths becomes exactly the difference of the two e_R terms (proof lines 230-251). Once that bookkeeping is done the numerical conclusion is a single citation of additivity of length, so the claim is H2.
